Post-fix the same payload is rejected cleanly: ``` REJECTED CLEANLY: format() output exceeds the maximum of 1048576 bytes ``` ## Changes - `MAX_FORMAT_OUTPUT_BYTES = 1 MiB` enforced at every append in `format_args` (template segments, argument renders, and escaped braces), via a small `push_capped` helper. - New `ExpressionError::FormatOutputTooLarge`. 1 MiB is ~6 orders of magnitude above real workflow usage, so no legitimate expression changes behavior. # Pull Request #143: feat: CI gate + auto-PR after successful CI State: OPEN Draft: false Author: @Bnjoroge1 Base: main Head: Bnjoroge/ci-gate-auto-pr Merge state: DIRTY Created: 2026-08-16T23:44:57Z Updated: 2026-08-18T03:20:18Z URL: https://github.com/preloopdev/preloop/pull/143 ## Body Three complementary flows for opening a PR on GitHub after CI passes on preloop: 1. Webhook auto-PR (server github_pr.rs): when a push-triggered run succeeds, server opens a PR per policy (auto: feature/always/never, draft, exclude patterns). Commit-message labels [no-pr]/[draft]/[pr] override policy. Dedup against existing open PRs. Best-effort async. 2. Dirty-tree flow (CLI + server): preloop run on uncommitted changes runs CI on the server snapshot. After green, interactive prompt [y/N/d] (or labels/flags) decides whether to materialize a real commit from the tested tree, push, and open a PR via push endpoint. Server accepts optional {create_pr, draft} override on push. Branch-head fallback for verification. Author = dev git identity. 3. Pre-push hook (contrib/): soft CI gate for committed pushes. Holds git push open while CI runs. [skip ci] bypass, resumable cache, fail-open when unreachable. Also: snapshot-tree exposure, dirty submission relaxed validation, config types, 8 new tests. just test-ci green. ## What & why ## Protocol surface - [ ] I confirm this change touches the runner protocol interface: **YES / NO** ## Required gates - [ ] `just test-ci` passes locally (fmt-check + clippy `-D` + full test suite + runner-watch conformance) - [ ] If protocol/wire shapes changed: the change is validated against the official runner (golden replay via `runner-watch`, or a live capture showing the official bytes), not only unit tests - [ ] If the touched subsystem has property tests (`concurrency_properties`, scheduling, matrix expansion, …): they are extended for the changed contract and pass (`PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server`) - [ ] New wire fields/events are additive and serde-defaulted where the official runner would not send them - [ ] No secrets, credentials, or internal/deployment-specific paths are introduced (captures with live tokens must be redacted or excluded) ## Verification performed ## Checklist - [ ] Tests added/updated for any new observable contract - [ ] Docs updated (`docs/`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`) where behavior changed - [ ] Changelog-worthy user-facing change described in the PR body --- ## Summary by cubic Auto-opens GitHub PRs after green CI on push-triggered runs and adds a pre-push CI gate. Previously only clean-tree `preloop run --push --create-pr` could open PRs; now webhook push runs can open PRs per policy, and the gate prevents pushing red commits while failing open only on engine outages. - Server auto-PR: Runs from native GitHub push webhooks open a PR per policy (`feature|never`), defaulting to draft, with anchored branch-exclude patterns; head-commit labels `[no-pr]`, `[draft]`, and `[pr]` override. It deduplicates existing open PRs, URL-encodes queries, skips local repos, and fires once at run finalization. Strict env parsing backs config, and recent hardening enforces provenance. - Push endpoint and dirty-tree correctness: `POST /api/v1/runs/:run_id/push` optionally accepts `{ "create_pr": bool, "draft": bool }` overrides; non-boolean values are rejected. For dirty submissions, the server records the snapshot `tree_sha` at accept, rejects runs without one, verifies the pushed branch head matches the tested tree, records `effective_sha` for webhook dedup, and skips submit-time checks for dirty pushes. - CLI and pre-push hook: `--push` accepts dirty trees, materializes the tested commit once before retries using the developer’s git identity, runs non-interactively when explicit, and the prompt reports CI outcome. The embedded pre-push hook gates only (never pushes), chains any previous hook, respects `core.hooksPath`, caches per remote/endpoint/sha with run-id resume, bypasses `[skip ci]`, handles all-zero remote SHAs, and fails open only on the `PRELOOP_UNREACHABLE` marker. Docs in docs/ci-gate-auto-pr.md; tests cover auto-PR, dedup, dirty-tree verification, webhook dedup, and hook lifecycle. **Rollout / migration** - Grant the GitHub App `pull_requests: write`. - Set policy: `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_AUTO=feature|never`, `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_DRAFT=true|false`, `PRELOOP_GITHUB_PR_EXCLUDE=pattern1,pattern2`. If you used `always`, replace it with `feature`. - The pre-push gate auto-offers on first interactive `preloop run`; to install manually: `cp contrib/pre-push .git/hooks/pre-push && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push`. Written for commit 55119f481736e7dea6dbd1aab8f9525fd9b11265.
